correctness.rationale: A complete marked-one-run bijection counts all n-vertex input configurations with fixed initial and updated support. One-step majority flips singleton runs only, giving P=H-s+t and the exact closed binomial-composition formula. All minority-coalition bounds follow from t<=r-1 and s>=max(0,2r-h), and the critical residue class enumeration lists all surviving tuples. Direct brute-force evaluation of all 2^n initial profiles for n=3..18 independently matches the entire formula; exact-composition sums validate the boundary multiplicities through n=101. Full infinite argument is combinatorial, not a finite experiment.

originality.rationale: The main contribution is the bivariate labeled one-step support-to-proponent distribution and exact multiplicities of minimum winning coalitions. Classical majority domination and Chebotarev–Peleg already motivate and partly cover coalition-existence questions, and the 232 majority local rule is known. The named comparisons distinguish the actual new enumerator from earlier existence and long-term-dynamics results; unindexed or inaccessible classical enumerations remain possible.

value.rationale: The exact bivariate census resolves the natural coalition-placement sensitivity of two-tier majority on a canonical fixed regular graph for all n. It identifies exact proportions of winning configurations conditional on coalition size and a nontrivial three-case quasi-polynomial count at the sharp minority-victory boundary, exceeding an existence-only or anecdotal example. The counts are applicable to exact probabilistic voting analysis without a broad-graph theorem.
